title: Nut-Free Cookies & Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with crushed nut-free sandwich cookies, ready in about 45 minutes from mixing bowl to cooling rack.
description: These cupcakes taste like a cookies and cream milkshake in cake form. I mix crushed nut-free chocolate sandwich cookies right into the batter, so every bite has little pockets of cookie. The frosting gets the same treatment with fine crumbs folded in for flecks of color and crunch.
ingredients: 10 certified nut-free chocolate sandwich cookies, crushed into chunks
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
8 certified nut-free chocolate sandwich cookies, crushed into fine crumbs, plus extra for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat 1/2 cup butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with milk and sour cream. Mix just until smooth.
Fold in the crushed cookie chunks by hand with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, beat 1 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar one cup at a time.
Mix in heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt until light and fluffy.
Fold in the fine cookie crumbs by hand so they stay visible in the frosting.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes and top each with a cookie half or extra crumbs.
tips: Check the package of your cookie brand every time. Nut-free certification can change between batches.
Crush cookies in two textures: chunky for the batter, fine crumbs for the frosting, so both layers feel different.
Chill the frosting bowl and beaters for 10 minutes before mixing. It helps the frosting hold its swirl.
Bake one test cupcake first if your oven runs hot, so the rest of the batch does not overbake.

faq.question: Which cookie brands are safe for nut-free baking?
faq.answer: Look for a brand that states certified nut-free on the label, not just gluten-free or vegan. Some popular sandwich cookies are made in facilities that also process tree nuts, so always read the current allergen statement before you buy.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a school party?
faq.answer: Yes. Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store them unfrosted in an airtight container at room temperature. Frost them the morning of the party so the crumbs stay crisp.

faq.question: Why did my cookie chunks sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: Chunks sink if they are too large or the batter is too thin. Crush the cookies into pea-sized pieces and make sure your batter is thick enough to coat a spoon before folding them in.

faq.question: Can I use gluten-free sandwich cookies instead?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as the gluten-free version is also labeled certified nut-free. Swap them in at the same amount and the texture stays close to the original recipe.

conclusion: These cupcakes are an easy pick for birthday parties or school bake sales where nut allergies matter. The cookie crumbs in the frosting make them look bakery-made with almost no extra effort.
